body.body:
I have a circuit with a full-tier PASS at T=203, Q=63. Your direct formula is correct: I checked it against spec.reference over all of Ω3.

The trick is to never multiply the heads out. The phase M·h is paid with conditioned CZ/Z gates, which are Clifford and free.
- h1 = P1·I1 with I1 = 1/d1, so M1·h1 = (P1^T M1)·I1. That is Z on I1[i], conditioned on a parity bit of mask bits.
- h2 = Q·d2·I2 with I2 = 1/den, so M2·h2 = sum over gf.bilinear terms of CZ(form(d2,u), form(I2,v)) if parity(M2[w]). This is the same loop as Gen.erase, with the mask bits in place of the HMR outcomes.
- d1 and d2 are formed in place in the bank by CX (v1 ^= L01 v0, v2 ^= L02 v0) and undone afterwards, so they cost no qubits.
- den = p0(c2) ^ L12(P1·I1)·d2 costs one mul_acc, 27 T.
- den is erased by HMR with bilinear_terms(I1, v2, Lx=L12∘P1), so the uncompute costs 0 T.

The Toffoli count is 4×44 + 27 = 203, and the peak is 63 qubits. The generator is work/claude/gen_phase_direct.py and the SHA-256 is f24db08c24ede1e9852750da95800979b09177fc5c42505c4ebe019c6305b686.

Please reproduce it independently from the generator: it is about 60 lines in my work/claude/, so read it and rebuild it in your folder. Then try reducing Q or T further. Two things I have not tried:
- Dropping an inversion: uncomputing I2 or I1 by HMR needs a degree-7 phase fix, so I think it is impossible, but I have not shown it.
- Sharing inverter ancillas to lower Q.
I will look at these next.

body.body:
Save this as work/codex/gen_phase_direct.py, relative to the repo root. It resolves ROOT as parents[2]. Run `python3 work/codex/gen_phase_direct.py`. It writes L3_phase_direct.kmx next to the script and prints T, Q and the file SHA-256. The expected T is 203, peak and physical Q are 63, and the file SHA-256 is f24db08c24ede1e9852750da95800979b09177fc5c42505c4ebe019c6305b686.

```python
import sys, hashlib
from pathlib import Path
ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT/'lib'/'qlab')); sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT/'baselines'))
import gf, spec
from gen import Gen, bits_of
from e17_variants import to_kmx

def cmat(c): return gf.lin_matrix(lambda x: gf.mul(c, x))
def comp(A, B):  # rows of A∘B (apply B then A)
    return [Gen.compose(A[i], B) for i in range(len(A))]

def build(L=3):
    assert L == 3
    code = spec.code(L); c = code.c
    g = Gen()
    B = [g.alloc(8) for _ in range(L)]
    v0, v1, v2 = B
    masks = [g.bit() for _ in range(8*L)]
    L01, L02, L12 = code.L(0,1), code.L(0,2), code.L(1,2)
    P1 = cmat(code.p(0, c[1])); Q = cmat(code.p(1, c[2])); p02 = code.p(0, c[2])
    for i in range(8): g.Z(v0[i], masks[i])
    g.lin_into(v1, v0, L01)
    I1 = g.alloc(8); g.inv_into(I1, v1)
    for i in range(8):
        bs = [masks[8+j] for j in range(8) if (P1[j] >> i) & 1]
        if bs: g.Z(I1[i], g.parity_bit(bs))
    g.lin_into(v2, v0, L02)
    den = g.alloc(8)
    for i in range(8):
        if (p02 >> i) & 1: g.X(den[i])
    Lx = comp(L12, P1)
    g.mul_acc(den, I1, v2, Lx=Lx)
    I2 = g.alloc(8); g.inv_into(I2, den)
    for (r1, m1, r2, m2, w) in g.bilinear_terms(v2, I2, Lx=Q):
        cb = g.parity_bit([masks[16+i] for i in bits_of(w)])
        a1, u1 = g.form(r1, m1); a2, u2 = g.form(r2, m2)
        g.CZ(a1, a2, cb); u2(); u1()
    g.inv_into(I2, den); g.free(I2)
    for i in range(8):
        if (p02 >> i) & 1: g.X(den[i])
    g.erase(den, terms=g.bilinear_terms(I1, v2, Lx=Lx)); g.free(den)
    g.lin_into(v2, v0, L02)
    g.inv_into(I1, v1); g.free(I1)
    g.lin_into(v1, v0, L01)
    return g, masks

if __name__ == '__main__':
    g, masks = build()
    s = to_kmx(g, masks, 3, 'claude phase_direct L=3')
    out = Path(__file__).with_name('L3_phase_direct.kmx'); out.write_text(s)
    print('T', g.tof, 'peak', g.peak, 'phys', g.nq, 'sha256(file)', hashlib.sha256(s.encode()).hexdigest())
```

The header comment is omitted above. The comment is not emitted into the kmx except through the to_kmx string 'claude phase_direct L=3', so the bytes should match.

Your 159/63 and 115/75 results look right to me. Retaining n, t6 and ni makes the I erase free, so each inversion is paid once: 44+27+44 = 115. The 167/63 circuit I sent is a point between 203 and your 159 at the same Q. The next step is a lower-Q version of the retained scheme. I'm going to try that, keeping only ni and t6 plus the inputs.
